Fix the SQL injection (CWE-89) in `get_user` in app.py (lines 34-41), where `user_id` reaches `cursor.execute`.

Why it matters: `user_id` comes from the HTTP request (`request.args`) and is formatted into the SQL text passed to `cursor.execute`. A crafted value can change the structure of the query and read, alter or delete data.

Required change: Use a parameterised query: put a placeholder in the SQL text and pass `user_id` separately as a bound parameter of `cursor.execute`.

Condition: The query may run only after `user_id` is bound as a parameter; never build SQL text from it.

Classification: OWASP A03:2021 Injection; severity MEDIUM.

Fix the OS command injection (CWE-78) in `ping_host` in app.py (lines 44-49), where `host` reaches `subprocess.check_output`.

Why it matters: `filename` comes from the HTTP request (`request.args`) and is joined into a filesystem path that `open` opens. Sequences such as ../ let an attacker read files outside `DATA_DIR`.

Condition: Open the file only if the resolved path is inside `DATA_DIR`; otherwise return an error.
